events.title: The first Swiss Guards arrive in Rome
events.description: A contingent of 150 Swiss soldiers arrived in Rome to serve as protectors of the pope, answering a request from Pope Julius II.
events.significance: The Pontifical Swiss Guard is still active more than five centuries later. It is one of the oldest continuously operating military units in the world.

events.title: The Battle of Rorke's Drift
events.description: A small British garrison at a remote mission station in Natal held off a large Zulu force in a fight that lasted into the night. The attack came just hours after the British army's crushing defeat at Isandlwana.
events.significance: The defense became one of the most celebrated in British military history. It earned a record number of Victoria Crosses for a single action.

events.title: Queen Victoria dies
events.description: Queen Victoria died at Osborne House on the Isle of Wight at age 81. She had reigned for almost 64 years, the longest of any British monarch up to that time.
events.significance: Her death ended the Victorian era and passed the throne to her son Edward VII. It marked a turning point for Britain and its empire at the start of the 20th century.

events.title: Bloody Sunday in St. Petersburg
events.description: Unarmed workers led by the priest Georgy Gapon marched to the Winter Palace to petition the tsar. Imperial troops fired on the crowd and killed many demonstrators.
events.significance: The massacre shattered many Russians' faith in the tsar and set off the Russian Revolution of 1905. It was an early step toward the upheavals of 1917.
